title: FixingPointSystem realism report
description: Report of the realism runner for one capture. Every check adds one entry to checks. A new check kind adds a definition under $defs and one if/then entry to $defs.check.allOf, and keeps the common check fields.

version.description: Report format version. Additive changes raise the minor version.

passed.description: True when checks is not empty and every check passed.

file.description: Base name of the capture file.

link_types.description: Link types of the capture, numbered as in the tcpdump link type registry.

skipped_frames.description: Frames that carry no IPv4 or IPv6 TCP or UDP packet the runner decodes.

metric.description: One metric value. The name is a metric of contracts/metrics/catalog.yaml, and labels are labels that the catalog declares for it.

failures_metric.description: The series that every check carries: the number of reasons for which the check failed. The label check names the kind of the check, and the value is 0 exactly when the check passed.

parser_errors_metric.description: Findings of one reference parser, in the sessions of one application or, with the application all, in the whole capture.

encryption_metric.description: The decrypted share and the JA4 matched share of the sampled TLS sessions.

content_metric.description: The duplicate share of the payload units of one application.

session_structure_metric.description: The rules that the instances of one scenario break.

transport_behavior_metric.description: The packets of one role whose field differs from the profile. A SYN has the side client and a SYN-ACK the side server.

conformance_metric.description: The share of the sessions of one application that the classifier names as the application.

temporal_metric.description: The KS statistic or p value of one comparison.

mix_metric.description: A share, a distance, or the largest distance of the mix that the classifier found.

check.description: Fields that every check carries. The allOf entries add the fields of each known check kind.

allOf.description: Every check of a kind that the metric catalog names in its label check carries the realism.check_failures series, which is 0 for a check that passed and at least 1 for one that did not. The catalog (0.7.0) names all ten check kinds (see contracts/changes/CON-23.md, CON-25.md, and CON-27.md).
Exactly one realism.check_failures series per check, which the definition of its kind ties to its own kind.
The failures series is 0 for a check that passed and at least 1 for a check that did not.

conformance.description: Share of labelled sessions that one classifier names as the intended application.

passed.description: True when at least one application was scored and every application passed.

metrics.description: The realism.conformance_ratio series of each scored application, and the realism.check_failures series.

accepted.description: Classifier protocol names that count as the application. An empty list fails the application.

observed.description: Session count per classifier protocol name.

mismatches.description: The first 100 labelled sessions that the classifier did not name as the intended application.

parser_error.description: One parser error with the session that it belongs to. A closed object where it is used, because the entries of not_counted add the fields rule and dissector.

name.description: The protocol of the faulty layer for tshark, and the weird names for Zeek.

expectation.description: One item of expect_findings in a session rule of the labels.

session_rule.description: Index of the rule in the sessions list of the labels.

item.description: A zeek weird name, or a tshark protocol with an optional part of the message.

parser_errors.description: Parser errors and malformed packets that reference parsers report, per intended application. The check passes when at least one parser ran, no parser reported an error that counts, and no declared finding is missing.

metrics.description: The realism.parser_errors series of each application and parser that ran, with the application all for the total of the parser, and the realism.check_failures series. When no parser ran, only the failures series is there.

parsers.description: The parsers that ran, in run order.

missing_parsers.description: Names of the parsers that the runner looked for and did not find. Report format 0.2.0 introduced this field, and skipped_parsers carries the same parsers with their reasons.

skipped_parsers.description: Every parser that the run skipped, which in auto mode is each parser that is not installed, with the reason. Empty when every requested parser ran.

parser_errors.description: The largest parser error count of any one parser.

malformed_packets.description: The largest malformed packet count of any one parser.

unlabelled_errors.description: Parser errors per parser in sessions that no labels rule names.

unattributed_errors.description: Parser errors per parser that belong to no TCP or UDP session of the capture.

errors.description: The first 100 parser errors in parser order.

errors_total.description: The parser errors that count, which is every finding except those of not_counted.

not_counted.description: The first 100 findings that the check left out of every count by a named rule, in parser order. Each entry is a parser error with the rule and the dissector that applied. The rule port_collision (RLM-19) applies to a tshark finding in a session whose client port tshark binds to a dissector and whose server port it does not bind to the same dissector. Reports before format 0.18.0 have no such field.

not_counted_total.description: The number of findings that the check left out of every count, which can exceed the length of not_counted. Reports before format 0.18.0 have no such field.

port_collision_ports.description: The number of TCP and UDP ports that the parsers bind to a dissector, from tshark -G decodes. It is 0 when no parser has such a table or tshark could not print it, and no finding is then a port collision. Reports before format 0.18.0 have no such field.

expected_findings.description: The first 100 findings that a session rule of the labels declares in expect_findings (RLM-20). Each entry is a parser error with the index of the rule in the sessions list of the labels. A finding listed here is in no count and does not fail the check. Reports before format 0.19.0 have no such field.

expected_total.description: The number of findings that a rule declared, which can exceed the length of expected_findings. Reports before format 0.19.0 have no such field.

missing_findings.description: The declared items that no session of their rule produced, for a parser that ran. Each one fails the check and counts once in realism.check_failures. A finding that no rule declares is not here: it is in errors and counts as before. Reports before format 0.19.0 have no such field.

unchecked_expectations.description: The declared items of a parser that did not run, which the check cannot verify. They do not fail the check. Reports before format 0.19.0 have no such field.

encryption.description: Decryption and JA4 check of a sample of TLS sessions. The check passes when at least min_decrypted of the sampled sessions decrypt with the exported keys and every sampled ClientHello has a JA4 fingerprint that its client profile lists. failures names each reason in words.

metrics.description: The realism.decrypted_ratio and realism.ja4_match_ratio series when sessions were sampled, and the realism.check_failures series.

tool.description: The program that decrypted the sample, or null when none ran.

embedded.description: True when the capture holds a decryption secrets block.

sidecar.description: Base name of the key log file that the run passed, or null.

labelled_sessions.description: Sessions whose rule names a tls_profile.

failures.description: One sentence for each reason that the check failed. Empty when it passed.

size_distribution.description: Size distribution of payload units in bytes. cv is the population standard deviation over the mean, and the quantiles use linear interpolation.

payload_group.description: Duplicate counts and size distribution of the payload units of one group.

content.description: Content variety of the application payloads. Every application has at most max_duplicate_ratio of duplicate payloads, the observed size distribution agrees with expected_sizes where the labels give one, and at least one payload was analysed. failures names each reason in words.

metrics.description: The realism.duplicate_ratio series of each application with payloads, and the realism.check_failures series.

ignored_headers.description: HTTP header names that the check drops before it hashes a message.

skipped_encrypted_sessions.description: TLS sessions, which the check does not read because it has no plaintext.

incomplete_directions.description: TCP directions with a hole in their sequence numbers, which the check cut at the hole.

truncated_units.description: HTTP messages that the end of the stream cut short and that the check dropped.

unparsed_tails.description: TCP directions of an HTTP session whose end did not parse as a message.

expected_sizes.description: The comparison with the size distribution that the labels expect, one entry per application with an expectation.

duplicates.description: The most repeated payloads, at most 20.

sessions.description: The first 5 sessions that carry a copy.

failures.description: One sentence for each reason that the check failed. Empty when it passed.

session_structure.description: Connection count and ordering of each scenario instance against the flow graph of its scenario. The check passes when at least one instance was found for every scenario, every flow has a number of connections that the scenario allows, every after edge holds (the later flow starts once the earlier flow completed), every spawn edge holds (the spawned flow starts while its parent runs), and the number of instances agrees with expected_instances where the labels give one. failures names the instance and the violated edge in words.

metrics.description: The realism.structure_failures series of each scenario, and the realism.check_failures series.

max_gap_s.description: Silence of a client, in seconds, that starts a new instance. Null when no gap splits instances.

sessions_unassigned.description: Sessions that match no flow of any scenario or that no scenario entry may claim. The check does not judge them.

server_port.description: Server port that the scenario fixes, null when the flow matches any port that no other flow fixes.

connections.description: Connections that the capture holds for the flow, over all instances.

failed_instance_details.description: The first 50 instances with a failure, with their connections in start order.

start.description: Capture time of the first packet, in seconds.

opened_by.description: Why this instance opened when the one before it had no room, or null for the first instance of a client.

start.description: Seconds after the first packet of the instance.

end.description: Seconds after the first packet of the instance at which the session completes.

failures.description: One sentence for each broken rule, at most 50. failures_total counts them all.

temporal.description: Inter arrival times, payload sizes, and packet gaps inside sessions against the target distributions of the labels, through the KS test. Each comparison is a pass when its p value is at least alpha, a fail below it, and insufficient_data when a sample has fewer than min_samples observations. A paced packet gap target (a constant with packet times) judges each stream on its own instead, and its p value is 1 when every judged stream passed and 0 otherwise. The check passes when there is at least one comparison and every one passed. failures names each reason in words.

metrics.description: The KS statistic and p value of each comparison for one application whose property the metric catalog names: inter_arrival, request_bytes (client payloads), response_bytes (server payloads), request_gap (gaps of the client streams), response_gap (gaps of the server streams), and packet_gap (gaps of both directions pooled), and the realism.check_failures series. Comparisons over all sessions, over both directions of sizes, and the paced comparisons of packet gaps (a constant target, whose statistic is not a KS statistic) have no series and are only in comparisons.

skipped_encrypted_sessions.description: TLS sessions, which the size comparisons do not read because the check has no plaintext. Zero when no comparison reads sizes.

application.description: Application of the comparison, or null for all sessions.

direction.description: Payloads that count in a size comparison, or the streams that a packet gap comparison reads, null for arrivals.

parameters.description: Parameters in seconds or bytes: value, mean, min, max, mu, sigma, alpha, scale. A paced target also has tolerance and within, and value only with one packet time. Empty for an empirical target.

values.description: The packet times in seconds of a paced packet gap target, null for every other target. Reports before format 0.16.0 have no such field.

source.description: Where an empirical target sample came from, null for a parametric target.

method.description: How the p value came about: exact, asymptotic, or constant. Null when the comparison had insufficient data.

reference_n.description: Observations of the target sample in a two sample test, otherwise null.

reason.description: Why the comparison did not pass, null for a pass.

streams.description: The streams of a paced packet gap comparison: judged (with at least min_samples gaps), failed, and too_short to be judged alone. The statistic is the largest share of late gaps of any judged stream. Null for every other comparison, and for a paced one with insufficient data. Reports before format 0.16.0 have no such field.

observed.description: Minimum, median, mean, and maximum of the observations, null without observations.

failures.description: One sentence for each comparison that did not pass, and one when the labels name no target.

messages.description: Message counts per session, read with tshark. Every session that a rule of the messages section selects has the expected number of requests, responses, commands, replies, or messages, every rule matches a session, and tshark ran. failures names each reason in words, for example a missing smtp message.

metrics.description: The realism.check_failures series of the check (metric catalog 0.6.0, contracts/changes/CON-25.md): its value is failures_total, so 0 exactly when the check passed. The check carries no other series.

tool.description: The program that counted the messages, or null when none ran.

rule.description: Position of the rule in the messages section, counting from 1.

expected.description: Expected count per name, such as requests, messages, commands.EHLO, or replies.250. A null max is no upper limit.

observed_total.description: The observed count of each expected name, summed over the sessions of the rule.

failures.description: One sentence for each reason that the check failed, at most 50. failures_total counts them all.

sessions.description: The first 100 checked sessions, failed ones first.

host_identity.description: The hosts of the capture and the IP addresses that send from more than one MAC address. A host is an IP address (not multicast, broadcast, reserved, or unspecified) that is the source or destination of an IP packet or the sender of an ARP packet, within one VLAN. The check passes when the capture holds no address conflict, the number of hosts lies in the expected range (when there is one), and at least one frame has an Ethernet source address.

metrics.description: The realism.check_failures series of the check (metric catalog 0.7.0, contracts/changes/CON-27.md): its value is failures_total, so 0 exactly when the check passed. The check carries no other series.

expected_hosts.description: The expected number of hosts, or null when the labels leave it open. A null max is no upper limit.

hosts.description: Distinct IP addresses per VLAN that appear as a source, a destination, or an ARP sender.

senders.description: The hosts among them that sent a frame with an Ethernet source address, leaving out the frames of gateway MAC addresses.

macs.description: Distinct Ethernet source addresses of those frames.

frames_with_mac.description: Ethernet frames with a station address as source, including those of gateway MAC addresses.

conflicts.description: The first 100 IP addresses with more than one MAC address, in address order.

vlan.description: The VLAN tags, outermost first and joined by dots, or null for untagged frames.

macs.description: Each MAC address that sent from the IP address with its number of frames, the busiest first.

failures.description: One sentence for each reason that the check failed, at most 50. failures_total counts them all.

transport_behavior.description: The TTL and the TCP options of the SYN and SYN-ACK of every connection against the operating system profile of the sending host. The check passes when no enforced field differs and at least one handshake of a profiled host was compared. The option order and the SYN window are enforced only when strict is true, and they appear in deviations either way.

metrics.description: The realism.transport_deviations series of each enforced field and role that the check compared, and the realism.check_failures series.

expect.description: The values of the labels that replace the profile.

profiles.description: The profiles that the check read, with the values it compared (after expect).

hosts.description: Each profiled host that sent a SYN or a SYN-ACK, with the profile it was compared with.

syns_total.description: Connections with a SYN in the capture, one per 4 tuple.

syn_acks_total.description: Connections with a SYN-ACK in the capture, one per 4 tuple.

unprofiled_handshakes.description: SYN and SYN-ACK packets from hosts that no profile covers, which the check leaves out.

deviations.description: Every field of a host and role that differs from the profile in at least one packet.

observed.description: The values that differ from expected, with the packets that show each.

handshakes.description: Packets of this role that the field was compared in.

enforced.description: False for the option order and the SYN window without strict.

failures.description: One sentence for each enforced deviation and for an empty comparison, at most 50. failures_total counts them all.

mix_row.description: One application of one basis. A share is null when its source has no total. A delta is the achieved share minus the configured share, in percentage points.

metrics_count.description: Sessions or bytes that the run metrics count for the application, null for the unmatched row.

ndpi_count.description: Sessions or payload bytes that nDPI assigned to the application.

reasons.description: One sentence for each source that is outside the tolerance.

observed.description: Only on the unmatched row: the sessions per protocol name that nDPI gave them.

mix_accuracy.description: The achieved mix, from run metrics and from nDPI, against the configured weights, per basis and application. Each source must lie within tolerance_points of the configured share. The row unmatched holds the sessions or bytes that nDPI named as no application of the mix and has a configured share of 0.

metrics.description: The shares that the classifier found in the capture, with source classifier, for the basis in metrics_basis, and the realism.check_failures series. Without a basis or an application with a share, only the failures series is there.

metrics_basis.description: The basis that the series describe, which is profile.basis of the test configuration, or the only basis that ran. null when neither tells it, for weights in the labels with both bases, and then metrics is empty.

test_config.description: The test configuration that gave the weights, null when the labels list them.

failures.description: One sentence for each broken rule, at most 50. failures_total counts them all.
